title: Compiler Flag Relaxation Causing Verification Holes
platform_conditions: tsconfig.json compile-time settings; strictNullChecks relaxation changes only the checker, emitted JavaScript runs wherever deployed
security_mechanism: With strictNullChecks off, the checker removes undefined from every type, so users[id] typed 'User' is believed non-undefined while the runtime lookup returns undefined for attacker-chosen IDs; the annotated return type then 'guarantees' a value the code never checked, and guards that look redundant are actually absent. skipLibCheck hides mismatched declaration files whose types disagree with runtime behavior, and path aliases can resolve a shimmed module -- the compiled output then imports something other than the audited implementation.

source_sink_clues.source: Lookup keys and IDs from requests, and configuration drift between tsconfig/lib types and the runtime the bundle uses.
source_sink_clues.sink: Index lookups and dereferences typed non-nullable under relaxed flags, feeding authorization or null-dereference-prone logic

tracking_guards: Check tsconfig enables strict (at minimum strictNullChecks), lookups on attacker-influenced keys are handled as possibly undefined at runtime, and declaration files for security-relevant modules match the runtime implementation.
not_candidate_when: Strict mode is on and the lookup result is narrowed before use, the key comes from a fixed internal set, or the failure path is non-security and contained.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: function get(id: string): User { return users[id]; }
synthetic_safe_example: function get(id: string): User | undefined { return users[id]; }
public_references: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
